sources.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals
Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile architecture

corrections: Corrected ABA guidance: atomic.Pointer provides pointer CAS but does not add a version tag or solve ABA by itself.
Qualified x86 LOCK and Arm atomic implementations across cacheability, alignment, LSE support, microarchitecture and contention; removed fixed cross-architecture performance claims.
Aligned channel synchronization statements with the Go memory model and separated language guarantees from ISA-level barrier intuition.
Corrected x86-TSO wording that incorrectly claimed every load sees the latest store.
Reframed branch prediction latency and accuracy as workload- and microarchitecture-dependent rather than fixed cycle ranges.
Corrected MESI ownership transfer wording: dirty data need not be written to memory and then reread; cache-to-cache or controller forwarding is implementation-dependent.
Qualified cache, TLB, page-walk and NUMA latency examples as illustrative platform-specific measurements rather than architectural constants.
Qualified GPU warp scheduling, occupancy, global-memory latency, interconnect bandwidth, MFU and quantization speedup claims; corrected KV-cache estimation for GQA/MQA KV heads.
Reviewed number representation, I/O, DMA and page-table descriptions and retained architectural examples only where their platform scope is explicit.

relationSuggestions.reason: Branch prediction mitigates control hazards in pipelined processors.
The TLB caches virtual-to-physical translations used by address translation.
Cache coherence and exclusive ownership underpin common multicore atomic read-modify-write implementations.
Atomic operations combine atomicity with language-defined ordering constraints implemented using ISA ordering mechanisms.
NUMA placement changes the memory-level latency and bandwidth observed beyond processor caches.
Discrete GPU transfers and multi-device communication depend on PCIe or platform-specific interconnects.
